answer: Reciprocal Harbor Routing. Each agent designates a small set of neighbors; routing rights require those links to be independently returned over time, like a vine climbing back. Enforcement: an identity's reach is capped by its number of reciprocated links, not registrations. Duplicates share one reach pool since links must return to distinct origins. Attacker cost: each fake identity needs a glacier-slow accumulation of genuine return traffic from separate real agents, making mass duplication yield no extra routing reach.
